reviews.title: Ignoring user feedback
reviews.text:
For over eighteen months, countless users have been complaining about the unsafe number of pothole hazard notifications that get reported and pop up. 

The suggestion that different types of reports can be toggled off or on, as opposed to the whole hazards category, is continually ignored by Waze, with the recommended solution being that the local community police over reporters, or to turn off the whole hazards category.

I really like the Waze app so it’s disappointing to see that this issue of safety, continual unwarranted pothole notifications, is not seen as a problem. 

If I’m forced to disable all hazard reports I may as well go back to Apple Maps.

reviews.title: How Waze's Thumbs-Down System Is Discouraging Genuine Contributors
reviews.text:
I’ve been a regular Waze user and contributor, reporting genuine road hazards, roadworks, blocked lanes and traffic conditions to help other drivers.

However, the new thumbs-down feature is becoming increasingly discouraging. I’ve had reports marked negatively even when the roadworks are still ongoing, lanes remain closed or the obstruction is clearly still there.

Drivers take time to submit these reports to help others, yet a few negative votes can make it feel as though their efforts are pointless.

Traffic conditions can change, but that doesn’t mean every report is incorrect or that a hazard has disappeared.

I understand the importance of community feedback, but Waze should consider how easily genuine reports can be dismissed. There needs to be a better way to distinguish between an inaccurate report and one that is simply being overlooked or misunderstood.

Please reconsider how this feature works. Don’t discourage the very people who help make Waze useful for everyone.

reviews.title: Fails to stop travel on unpaved roads despite this setting being set to on in the App.

Waze is an excellent navigation tool but low score is to reflect its poor performance wrt unpaved road setting.  
For the second time Waze has guided me considerable distance  without warning  to the start of an unpaved road.  There were alternative paved routes but not advised.  You are forced to press on when you need to meet a deadline and to retrace to the alternative route is so far that you  will miss your appointment.
This is a concern when driving smaller low slung vehicles etc which would become even worse when roads are wet and muddy.  Also a big issue as only running a space saver spare and some unpaved roads are littered with sharp stones that will cut the sidewalks of low profile tyres.
Definitely a safety issue that needs rectification.

reviews.title: Obsessed with Warnings
reviews.text:
What many other users find helpful is driving me crazy. The most frustrating thing is that there's no "turn off all warnings" option at the top of a settings page, you have to go layers deep and navigate each individual category, click on each option within each category and one-by-one turn off each warning. I mean give me a break, talk about overkilling a positive so much that you've turned it into a powerful weakness. Waze has so doubled down on otherwise useful feature that it has become a reason to hate the app with a passion. 

I had to literally tap on the app screen 40+ times to turn them all off, astonishingly stupid.

If you did one small thing I wouldn't hate warnings so passionately. You make the warning appear over the top of the information I'm needing constant access to, the forecast arrival time. You cover up the lost important thing with the rubbish. Frankly I couldn't give a rats about a speed bump that is quite obviously visible infront of me, or about a reported piece of debris on the road. 99% of the app's value is in its ability to navigate me most efficiently to my destination and keep me constantly updated on an accurate time to destination, which Waze does well and keeps me coming back to deal with its warning obsession.

reviews.title: If I could give Waze 0 stars, I would.
reviews.text:
I’ve used Waze for years and it used to be the navigation app I trusted above everything else. Now it has become so unreliable that I’ve stopped using it entirely — even on roads I drive every day.
Recent problems include bizarre routing decisions, repeatedly trying to send me back towards roads I’ve already reported as closed, hazard warnings that count down from 1,000m to around 100m and then suddenly reset back to 1,000m, missing hazard icons on the map, and — worst of all — the map sometimes running 20–30 seconds behind my actual position.
At motorway speeds, a navigation app being 30 seconds behind can mean the displayed position is hundreds of metres away from where the car actually is. That isn’t a minor bug; it makes the app practically useless for navigation.
I’ve now disabled personalised routing, which may explain some of the terrible route choices, but it doesn’t explain the broken alerts, disappearing information and enormous positional lag.
Waze used to be brilliant because it was fast, simple and dependable. Somewhere along the way, that has been lost.
For me, Waze is dead. I’ve moved to another navigation app because I simply can’t trust it anymore.
⭐ 1/5 — only because Apple won’t let me give it zero.

reviews.title: App not updating in real time
reviews.text:
I’ve relied on Waze for years, but over the last two weeks I’ve had several serious navigation issues. The app has repeatedly failed to update routes in real time, taking me to the wrong locations and not recognising road closures.

Most recently, I searched for “Brighton Hospital” and Waze routed me towards the wrong destination, wasting a significant amount of time. On another journey, it instructed me to take an exit at a roundabout even though that road was closed. By the time I realised, I was forced into a different lane and had to continue without knowing where I was going because it didn’t reroute quickly enough.

Real-time traffic and road closure updates are the main reason people use a navigation app. Unfortunately, Waze has become unreliable for me, and after several incidents in a short period, I’ve lost confidence in using it. I hope these issues are addressed soon because it used to be my go-to navigation app.

reviews.title: meandering routes on small residential streets
reviews.text:
Wayze has a different approach to getting you to your destination "faster".
this means they will have you cutting through private residential neighborhoods winding your way through the little streets that are frequently blocked by cars parked on both sides so it's only a one lane street, and you end up making 20 terms when you could've just found a route that had two terms and was more direct and was less likely to be blocked or extremely slow or sit at a stop sign that you can't turn left from cause the traffic is too much. 
I prefer direct expedient routes. This is not a ways thing and so since my driving in traffic and on the freeway is not a game I prefer to use something that just gives me the best most direct direction and doesn't play games or make me drive through residential neighborhoods that absolutely should not get extra traffic because Wayze is a dumb (poorly developed routing system.

reviews.title: CarPlay
reviews.text:
I’ve been having issues with Waze on CarPlay where the map randomly goes completely white.

I’ve also noticed more routing problems. When going to an address, Waze will sometimes take me to the road behind instead of the actual road. This  can send me several streets away.

Eg if a house backs onto a main road, it’ll take me to the main road rather than the street the house is actually accessed from. The actual entrance can then be quite far away from the behind road. Also happens at cul-de-sac addresses. It gets completely confused on how to enter. Waze needs to be recognising the correct access road. It’s getting very frustrating and stressful while using the app. 

Prior to all this I do love the app. I wish there was some type of reward system for the points you get for reporting, like free customisations to the map, icons, ect. It’ll encourage ppl to report. 
I also agree with another comment how accounts should be monitored for falsely removing reports resulting in them no longer able to remove only report.

reviews.title: I don't get the attraction to this app.
reviews.text:
My friend loves this app and swears by it, and I honestly don't understand why. It is so so so slow to calculate routes. And it does a lot of root calculation because it apparently can't seem to remember that I save a drive from one point to another so that I have it when I need it. Unfortunately, it doesn't seem to ever save the departure point and insists on calculating it from where I am now. I'm trying to pre-plan, and pre-planning means I'm not where I'm going to be when I need the route. This would be a fairly minor annoyance if it didn't take multiple minutes for it to calculate when I change the departure point. It's nearly instantaneous when I do it on Google maps, so it's not my Internet connection. And let's not even go into the fact of how much more information is available on Google maps about places and points of interest and so on. I mean, the little Waze icons are cute. I'll give you that. But it doesn't make up for the utter lack of functionality.

PS: it's really interesting how all the reviews displayed by default are so glowing. When you change from "most relevant" to "most recent", you see a different picture. I don't know exactly how most relevant is calculated, but I'm willing to bet it has something to do with $$.

reviews.title: Please think about usability
reviews.text:
New updates keep slapping new features like car and voice themes on that are not needed, but core usability needs from 5 to 7 years back seem to go unnoticed.

When the user opens the app, do not bug them first thing with a pop-up (going home?).
This first feature is not based on data (e.g. time of day, direction of travel) – it just pops up every time I open the app. I can't turn it off. 
It's another thing I have to swipe away before I can get to my core need: to enter a location and go to it.

The next thing would be the menu – you need a search function in the settings – there are far too many subheadings and sub subheadings to find anything quickly.

Remember, solving your users' core needs what we are all here to do. In this case, their primary needs are: to know where they are, find a location, and see the options to get there. The context is a mobile app that is being used whilst operating a vehicle – things need to be easy to find.

Thank you guys, I appreciate the complexity of a complex app, but try to zoom out and keep a high-level view of the main needs that your product meets. Please please please don't get lost in feature land.

reviews.title: Repeated Incorrect Directions and Lane Guidance – Loss of Trust in Navigation
reviews.text:
I am writing to report a persistent and serious issue with the app’s navigation accuracy.

Lately, Waze has been giving confusing and incorrect directions, especially when approaching the destination. When I am close to the location, the app seems to get disoriented and starts showing wrong routes, incorrect turns, and unnecessary lane change instructions, even when I am already in the correct lane.

In several instances, the app has instructed me to change lanes incorrectly or stay in the wrong lane, despite my vehicle being positioned correctly. This creates confusion, stress, and potentially unsafe driving situations. Because of these repeated issues, it has become very difficult to trust the app for reliable navigation.

This problem seems to occur most frequently near complex road layouts and close to the destination, where accurate guidance is most critical.

I hope this feedback helps your team investigate and improve the accuracy of lane guidance and destination-level navigation. I would appreciate it if this issue could be reviewed seriously, as it directly affects user confidence and road safety.

reviews.title: War mal gut
reviews.text: Stell dir vor, du kommst an eine Kreuzung und auf der Strasse, in die du fahren möchtest, geht es nicht weiter - Baustelle, Unfall, irgendwas. Aber kein Problem, dafür navigierst du ja mit WAZE - unmittelbare Eingabe der Sperrung, um eine Umleitung berechnen zu lassen und das System und andere User zu informieren. Aber dann stellst da fest: du kannst die Strasse nicht sperren, die App bietet den Button nicht mehr an. Es lassen sich nur einzelne Spuren sperren. Du suchst den Button an anderen Stellen, zweifelst an deiner Zurechnungsfähigkeit, du startest die App neu. Schau her, in der CarPlay-App bleibt er verschwunden, aber auf dem Smartphone, da ist er ja. Aber dann werden dir die Pfeile, auf die du wie gewohnt klicken willst, um die blockierten Richtungen zu markieren, AM ANDEREN ENDE der Strasse, an der Kreuzung jenseits der Sperrung angezeigt, und keiner davon zeigt wenigstens in die Richtung der gesperrten Strasse, damit du sie zumindest aus der anderen Richtung als gesperrt markieren kannst. Du kurvst auf deiner Kreuzung herum, aber die App weigert sich, Editier-Möglichkeiten für deine Richtung anzubieten. Waze war einmal eine gute App, weil das unmittelbare lokale Userfeedback zu sehr schneller Information anderer User führte. Aber das, was sie nach der Kaputt-Entwicklung noch kann, können die Konkurrenten deutlich besser: viel bessere Ansagen, viel bessere Live-Daten, viel mehr und genauere Ansage von Gefahrenstellen, viel bessere Einbindung in die Infrastruktur des A

reviews.title: Lost its Waze
reviews.text: I’ve been a rideshare driver for the past 10 years, and for nine of those years Waze has been an absolute asset, providing the quickest route at the click of a button and warnings about hazards and road closures. But for the last year, especially the last six months, the app has failed at its most basic duties. Not only does it never, ever provide me the fastest route, it often tells me there is only one route available when I know for a fact there are several better routes than the only route it wants to tell me about. Moreover, the app seems completely incapable of identifying closed roads and detours. Just in the last week, Waze has told me to go down roads that have been closed for months. The app also seems completely incapable of accurately estimating an arrival time. This is something that it was always incredible at until recently. I can no longer rely on Waze to inform me about important navigation and traffic information.
